## Architecture

`strivo-bin` is not a pure-data crate. Its `[dependencies]` link it
directly to the `strivo-core` workspace crate, the `strivo-plugins` workspace crate, the `strivo-web` workspace crate, the async runtime, CLI argument parsing, shell-completion generation, man-page generation, external-executable discovery, logging, OS config-path lookup. The list is read from `Cargo.toml`, so it tracks the
manifest rather than a hardcoded claim.

The crate's responsibility is:

1. Expose typed models and functions that a caller — the host, a
   sibling plugin, or the CLI — can drive directly (see `src/lib.rs`).
2. Keep the integration points above in one place, so the remaining logic
   stays unit-testable without a live runtime.
